title: Recover totals and interpret averages
chapter: Keep ratios, rates and averages precise
goal: Turn an average back into a total before doing anything else.

scenes.visual: Five stacks of counters of different heights are levelled until all are the same height. That common height is labelled "mean".
scenes.narration: The mean is what everyone would have if the total were shared equally. So a mean always hides a total: the mean multiplied by the number of items. Whenever a question mentions an average, recover the total first.

scenes.visual: Two class averages with a tempting "average the averages" crossed lightly.
scenes.narration: Averages cannot simply be averaged, and they cannot be adjusted without knowing how many items there are. Totals can always be added and subtracted safely.

scenes.visual: Four test-score cards with mean 7, and a fifth card face down. Text: "With the fifth score, the mean is 8." Question: "What is the fifth score?"
scenes.narration: Four scores have a mean of seven. A fifth score is added and the mean becomes eight. What is the fifth score? Pause and find the totals.

scenes.visual: Four stacks levelled at 7: total 28. Five stacks levelled at 8: total 40.
scenes.narration: Four scores with mean seven total twenty-eight. Five scores with mean eight total forty.

scenes.visual: The difference 40 minus 28 fills the fifth card: 12.
scenes.narration: The fifth score supplies the difference: forty minus twenty-eight is twelve. Notice it is much more than eight. One new score has to lift every existing score up by one, as well as reaching eight itself.

scenes.visual: Two groups: 2 people with mean 6, and 3 people with mean 10. Totals 12 and 30; combined 42 over 5 people gives 8.4.
scenes.narration: Combining groups works the same way. Two people average six and three people average ten. The totals are twelve and thirty, forty-two for five people. The combined mean is eight point four, not eight. It leans towards the larger group.

scenes.visual: A sorted list 2, 3, 5, 9, 31 with the middle value 5 circled as "median"; mean shown as 10.
scenes.narration: The mean is not the only average. The median is the middle value when the list is in order. For two, three, five, nine and thirty-one, the median is five, while the mean is ten. One very large value pulls the mean up but leaves the median alone.

scenes.visual: Lines: "Total = mean times number of items", "Work with totals", "Median = middle value in order".
scenes.narration: The total is the mean times the number of items. Do your reasoning with totals. And the median is the middle value. Notebook challenge: the mean of six numbers is nine. One number is removed and the mean of the rest is eight. Which number was removed?

notebook_exercise: The mean of 6 numbers is 9. One is removed and the mean of the rest is 8. Which number was removed?
